## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Ekapadajātaka* (Ja 238) is a story in the canonical Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework preserved in the text and commentary, the Buddha delivered the teaching while residing at Jetavana about a landowner residing in Sāvatthi [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. One day, as the landowner's young son sat on his lap, the child inquired about the "door to welfare" (*atthassa dvāraṃ*); recognizing that resolving this question belonged strictly to the domain of a Buddha (*buddhavisayo esa pañho*), the father brought the boy to Jetavana to consult the Teacher [Fausböll 1879]. The verse opening of the tale commences with the phrase *Iṅgh' ekapadaṃ tāta* ("Tell me one word, father") [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations across four languages [SuttaCentral].

Textual alignment computations by DharmaNexus show five segments of internal Pali text reuse between the canonical verses and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), including a continuous correspondence extending over sections §1.4–2.6 [DharmaNexus]. Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus records any external parallels or cross-language alignments in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
